To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the semantic web and grid communities are working on the same problems, and that the agent community can provide the missing link between them.

(i) agents and grids have a shared vision, (ii) agents and grids share a research agenda, (iii) semantic grid technologies can be used to create cognitive grids, and (iv) cognitive grids are the fabric for a future generation of intelligent systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and development of cognitive grids, a new class of intelligent systems that will enable a variety of applications in areas such as bioinformatics, e-science, and intelligent information systems.
creating a framework that will support the development of intelligent systems that are distributed, scalable, and self-organizing.
the design, construction, and evaluation of intelligent agents that operate in dynamic, open, and distributed environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantic grid is the most promising approach to the realization of the vision for a global computing infrastructure.
agents and semantic grids are complementary technologies that together will provide the fabric for a next generation of intelligent distributed systems.
the semantic grid is an agent grid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agents, grids and semantics can be combined in a way that will allow the creation of a new class of intelligent distributed systems that are able to adapt and learn from their environment.
we are building a semantic grid that can be used as a platform for the development of cognitive grids.
we have developed an agent-based framework for building cognitive grids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
agents are a good fit for semantic grids.
the semantic grid is a promising approach to building the infrastructure for the next generation of intelligent systems.
agents and grids are complementary, and that the combination can lead to a new class of distributed intelligent systems.
